newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Liberty key investments "not cast in stone".
newsitem.headline: Liberty key investments "not cast in stone".

text.p: The holdings of Liberty Strategic Investments Ltd (Libsil), which has stakes in some of South Africa's largest firms, were "not cast in stone", a Liberty Life director said on Tuesday.

Roy McAlpine, head of the asset management firm in the Liberty Life stable, told an investors' meeting that Libsil's holdings were continually being re-evaluated amid concerns about the share price's discount to net asset value.
"The discount to net asset value in recent years vacillated between 10 and 20 percent...It is quite within our power to unlock the discount at any time," McAlpine said.

Libsil's key investments include a 26.2 percent stake in Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd, a 23.5 percent stake in foods-to-retail group Premier Ltd and a 29.5 percent piece of Bevcon, the majority shareholder in brewing giant South African Breweries Ltd.
McAlpine said the Liberty group was discussing a number of alternatives for Libsil -- which he did not detail -- and would adopt the most beneficial strategy.
"Looking into the future are all Libsil's investments cast in stone? Answer: No, each one is consistently being evaluated," McAlpine said.

Libsil is a subsidiary of the Liberty Life group, an insurance and financial services giant with assets worth almost 120 billion rand excluding associates. Libsil was set up to hold investments considered too large for absorption within the group's policyholder portfolios.
